sentences.text: \paperprovenance
sentences.warrant: Retains the shared production disclosure verbatim. It is not a new review or publication approval.
sentences.section: frontmatter

sentences.text: A research repository can preserve a proof while losing the conditions under which its result was obtained. This paper describes a public Lean research repository that keeps questions, sources, proof attempts, papers and review decisions together. Python tools retrieve selected records, save proof checks and rebuild documentation. Two publication records serve different purposes: one connects a paper statement to registered formal supports; the other connects an explanatory passage to source excerpts and an authored justification. Neither automatically checks that the explanation follows from its sources. Researchers choose the work, and maintainers decide which changes to accept.
sentences.warrant: The cited entry, probe, resolver and passage-check code establish the named operations; the contribution guide assigns adoption to maintainers. The contrast concerns the distinct objects checked, not a claim that either record decides natural-language entailment.
sentences.section: frontmatter

sentences.text: In a historical author-run trial, publication checks rejected \HistoricalRejected{} of \HistoricalEdits{} deliberately false edits and accepted a false claim that an unresolved step was complete. We explain that failure, the limited follow-up, and the work still needed to assess whether the repository helps unfamiliar researchers.
sentences.warrant: The retained historical matrix records nine rejections and one escape, with only the escaped edit tested after repair. The reader-study file contains a proposed protocol, not completed reader observations.
sentences.section: frontmatter

sentences.text: When research resumes after a change of contributor, session or draft, the next researcher must recover more than the latest answer. They need to know which question was being asked, which assumptions a result needs, why an earlier approach failed, and where those facts were recorded. A repository can contain all the relevant files and still leave this reconstruction to its reader. The system described here makes selected relationships explicit and gives the reader a route from a short account to the sources behind it.
sentences.warrant: These are the documented design problem and intended use of the source-linked records. This paragraph makes no measured claim about reconstruction time or reader understanding.
sentences.section: Introduction

sentences.text: Consider a revision to a paper about Erd\H{o}s Problem~257. The unrestricted question asks whether every infinite subseries of a particular reciprocal series is irrational. The repository contains a theorem that answers this under a condition on the selected exponents. An editor could leave the theorem and its Lean proofs untouched while shortening its introduction to say that the problem had been solved. Every formal proof could remain valid, although the new explanation would be false. The condition, stated in Appendix~\ref{app:worked-proof}, is what separates the proved result from the open question~\cite{erdosproblems,paper257}.
sentences.warrant: The owning introduction states the open question and conditional result. The altered introduction is explicitly an illustrative editorial failure, not a reported historical experiment. Formal source is unchanged in this hypothetical.
sentences.section: Introduction

sentences.text: The repository addresses this problem with two records. A paper-to-proof record identifies the formal results registered as support for a particular statement. A passage-to-source record identifies the evidence for an explanation and preserves the author's reason for citing it. Checks detect changes to the recorded statements, files and source excerpts; a reviewer must decide whether the explanation is justified. The surrounding workflow saves attempts and review decisions so that a later contributor can inspect both accepted work and recorded failures.
sentences.warrant: The resolver compares statement identities and registered declarations, the passage checker verifies content hashes and nonempty warrants, and session/journal code saves entered attempts and decisions. Saving applies to records actually entered through those tools.
sentences.section: Introduction

sentences.text: The implementation discussed here is the public Erd\H{o}s research repository, organised around \ProblemWorlds{} problems. A separate verification repository holds selected formal challenges and comparison records. The public reading pages present material drawn from the research repository. A larger private working environment is outside this public implementation; a public clone does not require it. The account below concerns the supplied source snapshot, not the current state of a running service.
sentences.warrant: The public architecture, resolver repository check and frozen inventory distinguish the public repository, selected comparison repository and reading interface. Broader autonomy and private facilities are not attributed to the public clone.
sentences.section: Introduction

sentences.text: A researcher or agent chooses a task: investigate a question, check an argument, inspect prior work, or revise an explanation. The entry script uses that request to recommend instructions, source files and commands. It is a routing aid. It neither selects the research programme nor runs the whole task. For the illustrative revision, the useful starting request is to find the existing Problem~257 result and its unresolved boundary, before editing the introduction.
sentences.warrant: The entry function ranks routes and returns a packet of read targets and commands. The problem-registry route supplies existing reviewed families and boundaries. The example is a proposed use of those interfaces, not a new execution trace.
sentences.section: Choose the question, then retrieve its context

sentences.text: The lookup tools connect a problem to its reviewed claims, paper locations and declaration names. From there, the contributor can read the source paper or inspect a relevant Lean declaration and its dependencies. The retrieved record gives the contributor a starting point: read the claim, follow its paper location, then inspect its formal support. A missing route or an incomplete record leaves work to do, rather than establishing that no relevant result exists.
sentences.warrant: The query route returns family summaries, boundaries and declaration routes. Historical navigation descriptions distinguish selected indexes from completeness, so no exhaustive search or comprehension guarantee is asserted.
sentences.section: Choose the question, then retrieve its context

sentences.text: The files have different jobs. Lean source contains the formal definitions and proofs. The reviewed claim register records selected public assertions and their unresolved obligations. Paper sources contain the argument and explanation. Indexes and reading pages help find these materials, and are rebuilt from their source files. Editing a generated page directly would therefore leave the underlying record unchanged and risk losing the edit on the next rebuild.
sentences.warrant: Architecture assigns ownership to source files and structured registers; the projection builders regenerate derived files. The final sentence follows from that direction of generation, not from an automatic permission barrier.
sentences.section: Choose the question, then retrieve its context

sentences.text: There is no single complete graph of the research. The declaration inventory covers the imported Lean environment, while exact dependency indexes are built for selected roots. The broader interpretation index also includes descriptions inferred from context. A displayed connection can consequently mean a formal dependency, a reviewed support relation or a navigation suggestion. Its type and source matter. Adding a Lean module does not automatically add a reviewed public claim.
sentences.warrant: The documented index scopes and generated coverage distinguish inventory, selected dependency traversal, contextual interpretation and curated claim projection. No individual review is inferred for contextual descriptions.
sentences.section: Choose the question, then retrieve its context

sentences.text: For a proof task, the optional workbench sends a candidate Lean snippet to \texttt{lake env lean -{}-stdin -{}-json}. It saves the input, a content hash, the environment information and the last twelve lines of returned diagnostics. A probe is recorded as accepted only when Lean exits successfully, reports no errors and leaves no \texttt{sorry}. A failed proof, an unfinished proof and a timeout have different recorded outcomes. The next session can inspect the saved attempt instead of relying on a prose recollection of success.
sentences.warrant: The probe code checks exit status, error diagnostics and sorry count; session persistence records source and probe artifacts. Timeout or unavailable executable follows the error path, not kernel acceptance.
sentences.section: Check an attempt and save what happened

sentences.text: A contributor may then attach a claim to an accepted probe. The workbench verifies that the referenced probe exists and that its saved source still matches its hash. This protects the link to the attempt that was checked. It does not establish that the contributor's description is entailed by that source.
sentences.warrant: The claim operation checks accepted-probe identity and source hashes, while the claim text remains authored. The false completion sentence illustrates the resulting semantic limit.
sentences.section: Check an attempt and save what happened

sentences.text: A useful failed attempt records the question it addressed, the code or argument tried, the observed failure and the next unresolved step. A later contributor can use this account to decide whether to revisit the attempt or try a different approach. Contributors can also work through ordinary issues and pull requests without a workbench session. The journal consequently records only the work entered into it.
sentences.warrant: Session and contribution sources support optional records and multiple contribution routes. The suggested content of a useful failure account and its possible value are identified as method and unmeasured intent.
sentences.section: Check an attempt and save what happened

sentences.text: The Problem~257 revision reaches a different kind of task at publication. A valid proof answers the formal statement presented to Lean~\cite{lean4}. A paper also says what the result means, how it relates to the original question and what it owes to previous work. Those claims can change without changing the proof. The publication records separate these objects so that a reviewer can see which check bears on which part of the paper.
sentences.warrant: The two implementations act on distinct recorded objects. Lean is cited for its formal verification role; the example supplies the reason for retaining a separate explanatory record.
sentences.section: Statements, explanations and their evidence

sentences.text: The paper-to-proof record starts with an occurrence of a statement in a paper: its label, source location and text identity. It names the Lean declarations registered as support, at specified revisions. The record distinguishes exact support, support obtained by specialising a stronger result, support that depends on a named input, and a statement with no registered Lean support. The same mathematical result may have several paper occurrences, each with its own record.
sentences.warrant: The resolver and coverage schema bind labelled occurrences to pinned declarations and distinguish the stated support classes. Occurrence-level identities do not deduplicate mathematical results.
sentences.section: A statement and its registered formal supports

sentences.text: When a paper statement specialises stronger formal results, the author supplies a relation note explaining the connection to its registered set of supports. The resolver checks that this note was written for the current paper statement and the recorded Lean statements. If either changes, it requires review of the note. The note explains the relation of the paper occurrence to the whole registered set; it is attached to the coverage row rather than separately to each declaration. The supports are selected entries, not the full transitive dependencies of their proofs.
sentences.warrant: The exact_or_stronger branch checks a row-level note against the paper presentation key and a map of registered declaration stamps. No per-declaration relation-note field or proof-composition operation is implemented there.
sentences.section: A statement and its registered formal supports

sentences.text: Selected statements also have records from the separate verification repository. The resolver checks the named revision, entry, run and saved outcome, including the recorded Lean and independent-kernel acceptance and permitted axioms. Comparator checks a formal result against a separately stated formal challenge~\cite{leanfrocomparator,nanodalib}. Their scope is the particular statements and definitions compared; they do not establish that an informal problem was formalised as its author intended.
sentences.warrant: The resolver validates saved repository/run identities and the recorded kernel and axiom fields. Comparator associations concern formal challenge statements. No fresh replay or automatic natural-language correspondence is claimed.
sentences.section: A statement and its registered formal supports

sentences.text: The second record binds an explanatory passage to evidence. Each entry contains the passage text, source paths and line ranges, hashes of the source files and excerpts, an evidence class, and the author's justification for using those sources. An entry may cover several sentences or a displayed formula. The evidence class distinguishes implemented behaviour, a historical report, a proposed method and literature discussion.
sentences.warrant: The parser accepts multi-sentence marked blocks and the validator checks inventory, class membership, source identities and warrants. The evidence classes organize authored assertions; classification itself does not verify the truth of an assertion.
sentences.section: An explanation and its cited sources

sentences.text: The checker verifies that every marked passage has a corresponding entry, that the recorded hashes match, and that a justification is present. It does not decide whether that justification is sound. An author could update the hashes and write a false justification for the unrestricted Problem~257 claim, and these checks alone would accept the binding.
sentences.warrant: The validator enforces byte bindings, valid references and a nonempty string for the warrant. It contains no semantic entailment test. The false-warrant example is a direct consequence of those acceptance conditions, not an observed new mutation run.
sentences.section: An explanation and its cited sources

sentences.warrant: The two branches depict the objects and operations in the resolver and passage checker. The reviewer box identifies the semantic judgement left outside both tools; arrows do not compose proofs.
sentences.section: An explanation and its cited sources

sentences.text: For the illustrative revision, the editor should compare three things: the original open question, the theorem's hypotheses and conclusion, and the proposed introduction. The weighted condition restricts which exponent sets the theorem covers. The conclusion applies to every infinite subset of such a set and every integer base at least two. A faithful short introduction can omit the formula while retaining that restriction. It cannot turn a sufficient condition into an answer for all exponent sets.
sentences.warrant: The source statement supplies the finite-prime weighted hypothesis and hereditary all-base conclusion. This is a semantic review procedure for an illustrative revision, not a new mathematical result.
sentences.section: What the editor must still decide

sentences.text: The same review must retain the relation to earlier mathematics. Erd\H{o}s's reciprocal-summability criterion and Duverney and Tachiya's selection and averaging arguments are relevant antecedents~\cite{erdos1968,duverneytachiya,paper257}. The owning paper distinguishes their contributions from its weighted condition and additional averaging step. A list of proof links would leave that distinction unexplained. Appendix~\ref{app:worked-proof} gives the precise scope and credit without repeating the specialist derivation.
sentences.warrant: The primary-source closure records and owning paper preserve the distinction between the earlier reciprocal criterion, the selection/averaging method and the weighted refinement. The full mathematical proof remains in the unchanged owning paper.
sentences.section: What the editor must still decide

sentences.text: The paper tools prepare material for an author or editor. They collect a result's statement, supports, attribution and unresolved obligations into a bounded dossier. The short-paper tool audits labels, references, citations and coverage bindings, and can render a draft from that dossier. A separate assembler joins authored sections while retaining their references. These tools operate on supplied files without calling a language model. A person or external model drafts the prose, and the reviewer judges it.
sentences.warrant: Packet compilation selects registered material; the writer declares its offline deterministic audit/rendering scope; the assembler joins existing authored sections. No model invocation or mathematical transformation is attributed to these tools.
sentences.section: Prepare a draft without changing its evidence

sentences.text: An editor can work from a frozen packet rather than a live checkout. The packet records the exact input bytes, the files that may be changed and the expected return format. On return, the checker compares the input hashes and permitted paths, checks the required accounting, and runs the native manuscript checks on an isolated copy. A stale input or an unauthorised path is grounds for rejection. The checker uses its own native validation code, without running scripts from the return. It produces findings for the maintainer, who decides whether to apply the edit.
sentences.warrant: The refinement code freezes current file bytes and validates manifest hashes, edited paths and result accounting before native checks in a temporary copy. It does not integrate edits or execute returned validation code. A recorded Git head is context and is not treated as proof of a clean working tree.
sentences.section: Prepare a draft without changing its evidence

sentences.text: For the Problem~257 edit, the return would contain the revised introduction and its updated passage-to-source entry. The introduction would describe a sufficient weighted condition for irrationality, while the theorem and its formal supports remained unchanged. The reviewer would compare the revision with the theorem and the earlier sources before accepting it. This is an example of the review procedure, not an additional recorded trial.
sentences.warrant: Continues the explicitly illustrative editing task through its return and review. No fresh editing experiment or accepted integration is asserted.
sentences.section: Prepare a draft without changing its evidence

sentences.text: Permission to edit the live repository is separate from the kind of task being done. An advisory contributor can propose a proof correction, literature note or rewrite; an integrating maintainer can accept and apply it. The project calls these access roles Type~B and Type~A. They describe authority over files, not mathematical competence or independence. Ordinary issues and pull requests remain valid contribution routes, with maintainers responsible for deciding what belongs in the repository.
sentences.warrant: The public return protocol and contribution guide separate advisory and integrating authority from task type. No mandatory journal entry or independent reviewer identity is inferred.
sentences.section: Prepare a draft without changing its evidence

sentences.text: For contributions entered through the exchange, the research journal stores a sequence of events: the submitted return, its review, its disposition and any later correction. A return may be admitted, sent for repair, retained as rejected, marked duplicate or superseded. Earlier entries remain available. If a review is corrected, the new decision must be carried through to the records that used the earlier one; retaining the old event makes that dependency inspectable.
sentences.warrant: The journal schema enumerates these dispositions and models review correction and downstream invalidation. The operation applies to explicitly entered returns and reviews, not all Git activity.
sentences.section: Record a decision and rebuild the affected material

sentences.text: The journal checks event order and hashes linking each event to its predecessor. A file lock serialises cooperating writers, and an append operation checks the current head before writing. This helps detect broken or altered records within the journal. The lock does not cover transactions over every source file; someone with control of the files and checking code can also change both. These are limits of the local history as evidence, even when its hashes agree.
sentences.warrant: The verifier checks sequence and hash chaining, while the append path locks and validates before recording. The scope of the lock and local filesystem trust prevents stronger distributed or adversarial integrity claims.
sentences.section: Record a decision and rebuild the affected material

sentences.text: After a maintainer adopts a change, the affected source and reviewed records are updated before their derived pages. The refresh script has an explicit order for builders and then checks whether another refresh would change the outputs. It can run independent read-only checks in parallel. The order is intended to keep a revised summary consistent with the record from which it was generated.
sentences.warrant: The refresh implementation separates read-only checks from ordered writes and rechecks projection convergence. The causal explanation concerns stale generated output, not guaranteed global consistency or autonomous task planning.
sentences.section: Record a decision and rebuild the affected material

sentences.text: Publication checks and proof builds remain separate. The release script checks the configured publication requirements; it does not run Lean. The Lean continuous-integration workflow specifies the formal build. Both historical Lean source roots are subject to the same proof policy. That policy excludes \texttt{native\_decide} in the relevant checks; this is a local trust choice, not a claim that the mechanism is generally unsound. Appendix~\ref{app:repro} identifies the source files and commands for these different checks.
sentences.warrant: The release implementation and documented authority distinction separate publication checking from Lean CI. The historical mutation matrix identifies native_decide as a repository policy detector, not a general logical defect.
sentences.section: Record a decision and rebuild the affected material

sentences.text: A successful return check makes a proposal ready for review. The maintainer must still assess the mathematics, sources, explanation and credit before accepting it. The workflow does not technically force a second independent mathematician to perform that assessment. A second agent using the same selected context can repeat the first agent's mistake, so the number of recorded reviews alone does not establish independent scrutiny.
sentences.warrant: The contribution workflow assigns judgement without enforcing an independent mathematician. The same-agent architecture return provides a concrete reason not to infer independence from multiple workflow roles.
sentences.section: Record a decision and rebuild the affected material

sentences.text: An accepted revision may also suggest a change to the writing instructions. That is a separate decision: a useful edit in one paper may be poor advice for another. The project retains the proposed rule, the example, its limits and the integrating decision. Accepted changes revise documents or procedures used in later work. They do not train model weights.
sentences.warrant: The source-frozen refinement and public writing process separate manuscript acceptance, procedural lessons and later evaluation. No training mechanism or reader study is present in these operations.
sentences.section: Record a decision and rebuild the affected material

sentences.text: The retained inventory covers \ProblemWorlds{} problem collections, \LeanModules{} local Lean modules, and \Claims{} reviewed claims in \ClaimStatuses{} statuses, with \ClaimObligations{} recorded obligations. It lists \RegisteredPapers{} registered papers, including \ShortPapers{} short papers and \LongRecords{} long records. At journal head \texttt{\JournalHead}, there are \Rounds{} rounds, of which \RoundsSealed{} are sealed, and \Returns{} returns: \ReturnsAdmitted{} admitted and \ReturnsUnreviewed{} unreviewed. These totals describe the supplied snapshot.
sentences.warrant: All quantities are unchanged generated macros from the retained inventory. The journal categories and paper/module counts are reported as record counts, without inferring distinct new results or independent reviewer activity.
sentences.section: The repository inventory

sentences.text: The paper-to-proof inventory contains \LedgerRows{} statement occurrences: \LedgerExact{} with exact support, \LedgerSpecialising{} obtained by specialising stronger results, \LedgerNamedInput{} depending on named inputs, and \LedgerNoLean{} without registered Lean support. Of the \LedgerFormal{} occurrences in the first two categories, \LedgerCompared{} have a recorded comparison and \LedgerQueued{} are queued. The \LedgerWithLean{} occurrences with some Lean support include the named-input category. These categories count statement occurrences, not independent discoveries; repeated occurrences and overlapping supports prevent the totals from being read as a theorem census.
sentences.warrant: The generated counts partition occurrences by support class and distinguish comparison status. Repeated statements and overlapping support sets make unique theorem or novelty counts unsupported.
sentences.section: The repository inventory

sentences.text: The broader interpretation index illustrates a different counting issue. It attaches descriptions to \SemanticAuthoredInterpreted{} of \SemanticAuthoredTheoremLike{} theorem-like declarations, or \SemanticAuthoredPercent{}\%. Only \SemanticDirectEvidence{} are classified as having direct evidence; \SemanticContextual{} use contextual interpretation, and \SemanticStructuralOnly{} remain structural-only. The large coverage percentage must therefore not be presented as the proportion of declarations individually understood or reviewed.
sentences.warrant: The preserved generated macros distinguish direct evidence, contextual interpretation and structural-only entries. The paragraph explicitly prevents interpreting coverage as semantic validation or understanding.
sentences.section: The repository inventory

sentences.text: The historical publication-evidence record reports that \HistoricalRejected{} of the \HistoricalEdits{} deliberately false edits were rejected and \HistoricalEscaped{} escaped. The edits were authored by the checker's author, the original run logs were not retained, and the other \HistoricalNotRerun{} edits were not rerun against the extended checklist. Each edit was applied separately, restoring the baseline between trials.
sentences.warrant: The historical record supplies the ten independent mutations, nine rejections, single escape, author-designed selection and absent original run logs. It is not new execution evidence.
sentences.section: A false claim that passed the checks

sentences.text: The escaped edit changed an account of an unresolved step from ``does not supply'' to ``completes''. The publication checks accepted it. Table~\ref{tab:mutations} places this failure beside the nine recorded rejections: several checks detected changed coordinates, labels or counts, while the false completion sentence left those objects intact.
sentences.warrant: The historical matrix identifies edit 8 and the first detector for the other mutations. The contrast explains the recorded check coverage; it does not assign a numerical false-negative rate.
sentences.section: A false claim that passed the checks

sentences.warrant: Transcribes the ten-row historical matrix and each first detector. The caption retains authorship, missing original logs and the limited later follow-up; it is not a rerun.
sentences.section: A false claim that passed the checks

sentences.text: A later check was added for the false clause. The saved follow-up record reports that the post-repair witness accepts the current README and rejects a test copy containing the false clause. Here ``current'' refers to the baseline in that follow-up record. The other nine edits were not tested against the extended checklist, so there is no post-repair ten-of-ten result. The study locates a coverage boundary. Its nine rejections do not estimate how reliable the checker is.
sentences.warrant: The follow-up record contains baseline and escaped-edit results only. The explicit historical referent for current avoids presenting the retained witness as a fresh test of this revision.
sentences.section: A false claim that passed the checks

sentences.text: The trial used one corpus and the checker's own selection of errors. There was no manual-review control or comparison with ordinary continuous integration. It shows that these specific checks rejected these recorded edits and missed a consequential change in meaning.
sentences.warrant: The historical design lacks the named controls and independent sampling. The bounded interpretation is warranted by the matrix rather than a population-level experiment.
sentences.section: A false claim that passed the checks

sentences.text: On 23 September 2026, a maintainer-operated agent accepted one architecture handoff into a local integration history after focused checks of return routing and packaging. The same agent acted as contributor and reviewer. The record contains no live public pull request, independent mathematical review or outside-clone replay. It demonstrates a local path from a submitted artifact to a recorded integration decision, with those limits.
sentences.warrant: The retained return and contribution record identify the dated local handoff, same-agent roles and limited checks. It is not evidence of outside adoption or independent verification.
sentences.section: A local contribution handoff

sentences.text: Prove2Me is the closest comparison for collaborative mathematical work~\cite[Sections~3--4]{prove2me}. Its source-linked milestones pair a mathematical statement with a human-attested canonical formalisation. Its proof-sketch mechanism can compose verified subtheorems, with the parent verified only after its required subtheorems are verified. It also describes independent readback of formal statements and human review of the correspondence. These are substantive mechanisms for connecting a mathematical task to formal work. This repository's coverage row has a narrower role: it lists supports for a paper occurrence and records their relation to that occurrence. Listing those supports does not perform Prove2Me's proof composition. The additional passage record concerns explanations, including their historical and architectural claims.
sentences.warrant: Prove2Me v2 Sections 3.3, 4.2 and 4.4 describe readback, proof sketches and source-linked milestones. The local resolver and passage validator support the narrower comparison. This paragraph does not claim novelty for human review or statement/source alignment.
sentences.section: Relation to existing systems

sentences.text: Blueprints connect an informal mathematical argument to formalisation work. The Carleson project used its blueprint to initiate formalisation and revised it as that work exposed corrections and extensions~\cite{carleson,leanblueprint}. LeanArchitect attaches authored mathematical descriptions and metadata to Lean declarations, extracts dependencies and proof status, and exports material for a blueprint~\cite[Methods]{leanarchitect}. These approaches bring the mathematical explanation close to the formal source. The passage records described here also accommodate claims about a script's behaviour, a historical test or prior attribution. They record why a source is cited without deriving the explanation from Lean.
sentences.warrant: Actual reading of the supplied Carleson introduction and LeanArchitect ITP 2026 Sections 1–3, followed by verification of arXiv:2601.22554v1 Sections 3.1–3.4 on 2026-10-06, supports these mechanism claims in the edition cited. Public attribution records preserve citation identity, not execution evidence.
sentences.section: Relation to existing systems

sentences.text: The underlying techniques are established. Build systems track dependencies to decide which outputs must be rebuilt~\cite{buildsystems}. This repository uses fixed builder order and source hashes for a related purpose: identify derived records or explanations that need attention after an input changes. The extra relation note remains authored; a dependency check cannot determine whether the cited mathematics supports a new paraphrase. The repository applies dependency tracking to the continuing revision of research records and papers.
sentences.warrant: Build Systems à la Carte supplies the predecessor concept; local code shows fixed ordered generation and byte identity tests. The final distinction limits the novelty claim to this workflow and record arrangement.
sentences.section: Relation to existing systems

sentences.text: Souza and colleagues build an agent for querying workflow provenance, using a dynamically maintained schema to keep the language model's context smaller than the raw execution history~\cite{workflowprovenance}. Abedu and colleagues construct a repository graph from users, commits, issues and files, then generate and execute graph queries to answer repository questions~\cite{repokg}. Both connect natural-language interaction to structured records. Here, the journal records entered research contributions and review decisions, while lookup tools return selected mathematical context.
sentences.warrant: The supplied primary framework and approach sections establish the respective schema-driven workflow query and repository graph mechanisms. Local journal/query code establishes the different record scope. No performance numbers are transferred across tasks.
sentences.section: Relation to existing systems

sentences.text: Repository review itself is not new. The mathlib community describes contribution through pull requests and maintainer review, alongside public discussion~\cite[Section~7]{mathlib}. AGMAI's responsible-release guidance asks for understandable mathematics, appropriate credit, disclosure of tools and process, and accessible artifacts~\cite{agmai2026}. The records here can help a reviewer inspect some of that information. They do not certify compliance with the whole guidance, supply an independent review, or turn formal validity into a judgement of mathematical importance.
sentences.warrant: The mathlib CPP 2020 contribution section and AGMAI 29 September 2026 guidance supply the cited predecessors. Local credit and contribution files describe inspectable records, with no external approval or compliance certificate.
sentences.section: Relation to existing systems

sentences.text: The main uncertainty is whether this organisation helps someone who did not build it. No independent reader study, adoption by another laboratory, discovery-rate comparison or measured reduction in review cost is reported. Nor has the system been compared with a well-maintained repository containing a good README and ordinary continuous integration. More records and more links may reduce reconstruction work, or may merely add another layer to maintain. The inventory cannot decide between those possibilities.
sentences.warrant: The evaluation file and strategy sources contain proposed studies and explicit unmeasured outcomes. Counts show scale of stored records only. The alternatives are hypotheses, not empirical findings.
sentences.section: Limits and the next evaluation

sentences.text: A useful first evaluation would give unfamiliar researchers fixed tasks: find the result answering a question, recover a necessary hypothesis, identify the relevant prior work, or diagnose a discrepancy between a paper and its record. Compare ordinary repository browsing with an information-equivalent static brief and with the navigation tools. Holding the available information constant would help separate the benefit of selection from the benefit of the interface. Record wrong conclusions, omitted conditions, unresolved tasks and requests for help, as well as completion time.
sentences.warrant: The supplied reader-study and evaluation proposals motivate bounded task comparisons. The information-equivalent static-brief condition is a proposed control, with no participants, results or effect estimates implied.
sentences.section: Limits and the next evaluation

sentences.text: The evaluation should include the cost of preparing records, keeping them current and repairing misleading entries. It should retain timeouts, failed attempts and reviewer disagreement, rather than reporting only successful tasks. Yuan and colleagues' study of open-hardware documentation offers a relevant test of the premise: unfamiliar students followed existing procedures and exposed ambiguities, missing practical detail and obsolete tooling~\cite{documentationtest}. That study concerns people using hardware documentation, not an automated check of explanatory prose. An equivalent outside-reader test of this repository remains to be done.
sentences.warrant: The proposed cost accounting is supported by the evaluation plan. Actual inspection of Yuan et al. Sections 1–3 and 5–6 establishes the bounded documentation comparison. No automatic documentation checker or local reader result is attributed to that source.
sentences.section: Limits and the next evaluation

sentences.text: The public workflow also depends on explicit choices: someone must choose a worthwhile task, enter useful evidence and accept or reject its result. It does not provide an autonomous research scheduler. Volunteer computation, transfer to other sciences and a broader service for coordinating researchers remain proposals. No upstream mathlib contribution from this workflow is established by the retained records, and possible exposure of the source material during model training is unknown. These uncertainties should be resolved before attributing new discoveries or efficiency gains to the system.
sentences.warrant: The historical strategy distinguishes goals from implemented public operations and records limits on adoption, upstream contribution and model-training exposure. The paragraph does not convert those proposals into public capabilities.
sentences.section: Limits and the next evaluation

sentences.text: This repository makes selected research records easier to inspect together: the question, attempted work, formal support, explanation and review decision. Its important design choice is to preserve the difference between them. The escaped completion claim shows why that distinction matters. A changed hash directs the reviewer to material that needs attention; a formal check establishes its specified formal statement. Someone still has to decide whether the paper says what the evidence permits. The next test is whether these records help an unfamiliar researcher make that decision accurately and at reasonable cost.
sentences.warrant: Synthesizes the implemented arrangement and recorded failure without claiming measured readability or research gains. The concluding evaluation is prospective.

sentences.text:
Let $A$ be an infinite set of positive integers and $P$ a finite nonempty set of primes. Write $h_P(a)$ for the largest divisor of $a$ whose prime factors lie in $P$. The owning paper proves the following sufficient condition~\cite{paper257}:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:worked-condition}
 W_{2,P}(A):=\sum_{a\in A}\frac{h_P(a)}{a(2^{h_P(a)}-1)}<\infty
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \sum_{a\in B}\frac{1}{b^a-1}\notin\mathbb Q
\end{equation}
for every infinite $B\subseteq A$ and every integer $b\ge2$. The base-two condition implies the corresponding condition at every larger base. A condition imposed only at a fixed base gives the fixed-base conclusion; it should not silently be turned into an all-base assertion. The unrestricted Problem~257 remains open in this work.
sentences.warrant: The theorem retains infinite positive-integer support, finite nonempty prime set, weighted binary summability, hereditary quantifier and all integer bases. It restates the existing example, with no new proof work or change to owning mathematical sources.
sentences.section: The condition in the Problem 257 example

sentences.text: Erd\H{o}s proved an earlier irrationality criterion under pairwise coprimality and reciprocal summability, and stated that the coprimality restriction could be removed without supplying the details of that extension there~\cite{erdos1968}. The owning paper gives the extension argument. Duverney and Tachiya supply relevant selection and congruence ideas and the first averaging step~\cite{duverneytachiya}. The weighted proof adds an average over dyadic progression lengths; this supplies the factor $1/a$ needed in the displayed condition. Its proof, parameter choices and a separating example are in the Problem~257 paper, rather than repeated here~\cite[Section~2]{paper257}. The separating example's calculation is an ordinary argument, not a separately registered Lean result.
sentences.warrant: The source-closure records identify the earlier theorem and unproved extension assertion; the owning proof identifies the additional average. The ordinary separating example is not promoted to an independently formalised result.

sentences.text: Three other records illustrate why attribution and scope need their own review. They are not additional systems experiments. In Problem~269, the result concerns distinct running least common multiples; the original question counts repeated values with multiplicity. The paper credits Fan's earlier public two-prime result despite a reported independent derivation, and identifies the related Hecke--Mahler literature~\cite{paper269,fan269,loxtonvdp1977,bugeaudlaurent2023}. Neither formalisation nor independent derivation removes that earlier credit.
sentences.warrant: The owning introduction preserves distinct-value versus multiplicity scope and the priority credited to Fan. This is a condensed attribution record, not a new mathematical derivation.

sentences.text: For Problem~249, the paper gives explicit reductions and an integral basis for relations among totient subsequences~\cite{paper249}. Coons establishes non-regularity, while Martin's stronger separation result already implies the independence used for the basis. The direct argument uses the Chinese remainder theorem and Dirichlet's theorem through an argument in Yazdani, who credits Shallit~\cite{coons,martin,yazdani}. The explicit description, the inherited independence result and its formalisation are distinguishable contributions.
sentences.warrant: The owning introduction gives the exact contribution hierarchy and credit chain. This removes specialist notation while preserving which antecedent implies the needed independence.

sentences.warrant: The coverage and reviewed results introduction retain ani attribution, the exact formal target, four registered supports, pending Comparator, absent independent historical correspondence review and the seven remaining unresolved targets.
